title.narrative: Output 4.3. Increased capacity of member States to develop policies, legislation and other measures that are specifically aimed at facilitating the transition of enterprises to formality

description.narrative:
From March 2020, the National Bureau of Statistics conducted National Informal Sector Diagnostic Survey to inform policies, strategies and plans to facilitate the transition of enterprises to formality, the survey report included policy brief on the options to deal with informality. The survey started with Dar es Salaam which was finalized in October 2020, The report has been published and disseminated.
The Government through Tanzania Cooperative Development Commission reviewed the Cooperative Development Policy, November-December 2020, with the aim of creating an enabling environment for cooperatives as autonomous, member-owned, and democratically-controlled enterprises With the support from UN fund; TZA/17/03/OUF, ILO provided technical supports to conduct Dar es Salaam Informal Sector Survey in 2020. The support extended to the National Bureau of Statistics includes design of survey instruments sampling design, analysis, report writing and publication of the survey report.
ILO further, using same resources of TZA/17/03/OUF contributed to enhanced integration of decent work principles in the revised draft Cooperative Development Policy, including ensuring a strong focus on the importance of data collection and usage, building on best practices, human development and integration of gender and youth concerns.

Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
The Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE) in August 2020 adopted the ILO productivity improvement programme for Small and Medium Scale enterprises (SMEs) called Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE). The programme focuses on building national capacity to implement productivity improvement in the targeted SMEs in manufacturing sub-sector. From this intervention 5 medium-sized enterprises with over 600 workers have benefitted from this support through enhanced workplace relations, safer, more efficient and productive workplaces, competitiveness, growth and better jobs as well as improved compliance to labour laws.
The Tanzania Association of Professional Business Development Services (TAPBDS), in May 2020, introduced tailor made non-financial Business Development Services (BDS); Start and Improved Your Business (SIYB) to self- employed, micro and small enterprises targeting young women & men
A strategic partnership to address structural drivers of the HIV/AIDS epidemic was established. In 2020- 2021, under Employment Intensive Investment Program (EIIP) and Tanzania Social Assistance Fund (TASAF), the local authorities and Start and Improve Your Business Association of East Africa ahve trained about 200 youth (112 females and 88 males) from TASAF's Productive Social Safety Net (PSSN). The programme beneficiary households have been selected by Local Government Authorities. With support from One Fund, TZA/17/03/OUF the ILO developed the capacity of ATE to co-ordinate SCORE at national level through Technical Training of Trainers and Coaching and mentoring support. ILO also supported certification of trainers, who trained on SCORE.
With resources from UN joint Program; TZA/17/03/OUF, ILO provided technical training of trainers on ILO’s SIYB training programme to enhance the capacity of 12 local BDS providers, 2 Financial Institutions and 6 Local Government Authorities (from August 2020), to deliver market oriented and gender-responsive enterprise development trainings. This is addition to direct interventions to support the capacity of selected youth and women entrepreneurs (2,712) to plan their businesses and access capital for small-scale investment.
The ILO facilitated a strategic partnership using resources of the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS; GLO/20/09/UNA and in equipping young women and men from poor household families with adequate entrepreneurship knowledge and skills to enable them to tap on the income opportunities from locally available resources and enhanced knowledge and skills on HIV prevention strategies and mitigation measures
